outcome: No result changing the status of the Nagata-Biran conjecture (Seshadri constant ε(p1,...,pr;X,L) = d/√r for large r, on a smooth algebraic surface X with ample L of degree d) was found in the window 26 January 2024 to 22 September 2026.
summary: The Nagata-Biran conjecture generalizes Nagata's conjecture (on very general points in P^2) to an arbitrary smooth projective surface X with an ample line bundle L: for sufficiently large r, the r-point Seshadri constant equals the maximal possible value d/√r. As of January 2024 this was already known only asymptotically (verified as r→∞ up to lower-order terms, by Biran/Biran-Szemberg and, by different methods, by Harbourne), and it remains in that state today. Extensive searching (arXiv listings, Google/web search across many query variants, the Wikipedia articles for both 'Seshadri constant' and 'Nagata-Biran conjecture', and recent papers on Seshadri constants and symplectic embeddings) turned up no paper, preprint, or announcement in the 26 January 2024 - 22 September 2026 window that proves the conjecture for a general surface, extends the asymptotic verification, or narrows the class of surfaces for which it is open. Related but distinct work exists: a February 2025 paper on the 'valuative Nagata conjecture' (a strengthened variant of the classical, planar Nagata conjecture, not the surface-general Nagata-Biran statement); a May 2026 paper 'Weighted Seshadri constants and ellipsoid embeddings' (arXiv:2605.27574) that builds machinery from the McDuff-Schlenk staircase and speculates it might eventually be relevant to proving the classical (P^2) Nagata conjecture, but explicitly does not resolve it and does not address the general surface case; and continuing work on multi-point Seshadri constants on special surface classes (e.g. ruled surfaces) that gives explicit bounds/values in special cases but is framed as verifying expected behavior on those surfaces, not as new territory toward the general conjecture. None of this constitutes a case of, or progress on, the Nagata-Biran conjecture as stated (a general smooth surface and ample L), so status is 'open' with no_change_found true. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature; all identified work is conventional human mathematical research.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2026 weighted-Seshadri-constant paper's remark that its infinite sequence of divisors 'is precisely what one needs to prove the Nagata conjecture' constitutes 'progress' worth recording even though it is speculative and about the classical planar case rather than the general Nagata-Biran statement. I judged this a related/variant problem (the classical Nagata conjecture on P^2, which is itself a special case one level below the Nagata-Biran generalization, and the remark is prospective/speculative rather than an actual advance) rather than a case or resolution of the bullet as stated, so it does not change the status.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving the exact asymptotic (not just up-to-lower-order-terms) formula ε = d/√r for large r on a general smooth surface X with ample L, or extending the known asymptotic verification to a strictly larger class of surfaces than was already covered before January 2024, would count as progress; a full proof for arbitrary X and L would resolve it.
